cohort: 225 girls (201 cases and 201 controls) and 120 boys (24 cases and 96 controls)
finding: Cesarean section, child BMI, maternal BMI, and exposure to secondhand smoke were risk factors for precocious puberty in girls, while maternal height, paternal height, bedtime at night, and night sleep were protective factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a risk factor for precocious puberty in girls.
